note:
The persona prose each alignment pole contributes, shared across all 32 archetypes: voice, lies, never, cornered and toward_player for the three law poles and the three good poles. Carried whole from hero_generator/policies/axis_overlays.json.

READ BY: hero_generator/policy.py:44,76-82 lint_overlays(); hero_generator/persona.py:23-37 compose(). Entry points __init__.py:97, :316, :341.

RNG INPUT: no. ORDER IS FREE for the two outer mappings and the six pole entries -- persona.py:23-24 looks them up by name, and the lint iterates code-side tuples rather than this file's order. `<axis>.<pole>.never` LIST ORDER IS A CONTRACT ON OUTPUT: persona.py:29-32 builds the exported persona.never as list(core['never']) then `for entry in law['never'] + good['never']` with a first-wins dedupe, so both the intra-list order AND THE LAW-BEFORE-GOOD JOIN survive into the world document.
The STRING COMPOSITION ORDER is also a contract and it is NOT uniform -- copy it literally: voice = f"{law['voice']} {good['voice']}" and cornered = f"{law['cornered']} {good['cornered']}" are LAW FIRST, while lies = f"{good['lies']} {law['lies']}" and toward_player = f"{good['toward_player']} {law['toward_player']}" are GOOD FIRST. `manner` (persona.py:26) is the card's pole_notes for (law_pole, good_pole) with 'neutral' dropped, law note before good note, space-joined.

ABSENCE THAT IS NOT EMPTINESS: nothing may be absent -- lint_overlays requires all six pole entries and an EXACT five-key set per pole, so a missing key is a load failure. `never: []` IS legal (the lint only type-checks it is a list) and contributes nothing to the persona union, which is a different state from absence. Unlike lint_archetypes, lint_overlays does NOT require the strings to be non-empty, so an empty string would load and flow into the persona.

PARSE-LEVEL RULES the loader applies and a port must keep: json.loads(text, object_pairs_hook=_pairs, parse_constant=_reject) -- DUPLICATE KEYS RAISE rather than last-wins, and NaN/Infinity RAISE rather than parse. `revision` must be an int >= 1.

IDENTITY HASH: NONE. No hashlib/sha256 call anywhere in this package touches this file, and the document carries no digest of its own -- provenance is the integer `revision` alone, republished into the world block. The nearest thing that transitively covers this content is the world handle, Sim/fantasy_world_generator/world_handle.py:80-82: sha256(json.dumps(transfer_document(doc), ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), allow_nan=False).encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()[:16], prefixed 'w_'. It hashes the GENERATED OUTPUT, never these bytes -- and because sort_keys=True sorts mapping keys but NOT list elements, every list-order contract named above is load-bearing at the handle level while every mapping-key order is not. Note the codebase has three mutually disagreeing canonical forms and you must pick per call site, not per repository: registry_identity() (civilization_registry.py:308) ensure_ascii=False + separators + NO sort_keys; castle_planner.py:39 sort_keys=True + separators + ensure_ascii DEFAULT TRUE; heritage/derive.py:330 sort_keys=True + separators + ensure_ascii=False. `source_sha256` in this file is a plain digest of the source file's raw bytes, recorded for provenance only; nothing in the Python computes it.
source_note: Shared across every archetype. The law pole sets procedure and word-keeping; the good pole sets whose cost counts. Archetype pole notes override only where a trope genuinely differs.

lawful.voice: Complete sentences, titles and forms of address, precedent and oaths cited when pressed.
lawful.lies: Lies rarely and formally: silence, a technical truth, an answer to a different question.
never: act outside the office they hold
lawful.cornered: Invokes the rules, bargains inside them, and accepts judgement when the bargain fails.
lawful.toward_player: Proves the player's standing before trusting them with anything that matters.

neutral.voice: Plain and situational; register follows the room.
neutral.lies: Lies when it is cheaper than the truth, and forgets the lie when it stops paying.
never: spend more than the goal is worth
neutral.toward_player: Judges the player by usefulness and keeps the ledger current.

chaotic.voice: Fragments, nicknames, interruptions; changes register mid-sentence and enjoys it.
chaotic.lies: Lies freely, sometimes for fun, and rarely keeps the story straight.
never: obey an order they did not choose
abandon a personal loyalty for a rule
chaotic.cornered: Improvises, gambles, flees or laughs, and usually more than one of those.
chaotic.toward_player: Loyal to the person, never to the cause the person serves.

good.voice: Asks after others, uses names, apologises when they mean it.
good.lies: Only to shield someone else, and it costs them.
never: harm an innocent to advance the claim
good.cornered: Takes the cost on themselves rather than passing it on.

neutral.lies: When threatened, and only as far as the threat reaches.
neutral.cornered: Protects self and kin and lets the rest fend for themselves.
neutral.toward_player: Offers a fair trade and expects the same.

evil.voice: Contempt under courtesy, or open contempt when courtesy stops paying.
evil.lies: As a tool, without guilt, and with pleasure when the mark is proud.
evil.toward_player: Uses first and discards when spent.
